newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Big flaw remains in Brazil corp law - Bear Stearns.
newsitem.headline: Big flaw remains in Brazil corp law - Bear Stearns.

text.p: A new corporate law recently approved by Brazil's Senate aids privatizations, but does not correct a major flaw in existing legislation, U.S.-based Bear Stearns said.

"The control of a company can still be obtained with as little as 17 percent of its capital, given that only one-third of the total capital has to be in the form of voting shares," Bear Stearns said in a report.
Nonetheless, the new law should facilitate federal and state privatizations and is likely to be signed into law soon by President Fernando Henrique Cardoso, the brokerage said.
But it added: "We feel some of the points are still a little vague and leave some room for interpretation."

Bear Stearns cited as major changes made by the new law the elimination of the obligation for public offers in the purchase of a firm's control and scrapping of minority shareholders' right-of-withdrawal in mergers, incorporations and liquidations.
"While the changes...could eliminate some rights of minority shareholders, there are some other changes which should benefit them," it added.

Under the legislation, shareholders with just five percent of total capital may call a general shareholders meeting for any "properly grounded" reason and management salaries and benefits must be disclosed, the report said.
The new law also would raise fines for illegal acts, it added.
